solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mother — look — has collected popular periodical

parts.note: MA is an everyday word for mother

indicators.note: the word for look gathers up the word for popular inside itself

parts.note: to gaze is to look steadily
IN means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A mother glances over a popular journal she has picked up.
explanation.definitionFit: A periodical publication, issued weekly or monthly, is a synonym for this.

clue.text: Criminal pinches a dress and money container

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked or bent, so the letters of the following words are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A crook steals a frock along with a cash box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like the subject of 'pinches', but it signals that PINCHES, A and DRESS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash machine at a bank is literally a box that holds and dispenses money, described playfully.

clue.text: Dosage adjusted for old sailor

indicators.note: the letters of the medicine word are adjusted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A doctor alters a veteran mariner's medication.
explanation.definitionFit: A seasoned, experienced mariner is idiomatically called this.

clue.text: Notice captain covering very cold region

indicators.note: the two words cover the answer, holding it within their letters

explanation.surface: A posted notice tells the ship's master he is responsible for a frozen zone.
explanation.definitionFit: A polar sheet of permanent ice is a region of extreme cold.

clue.text: Imitating skier, maybe, past his best

definitions.meaning: a skier typically descends a slope, so this is literally heading down a slope
the idiom for declining or deteriorating

explanation.surface: An ageing athlete is mocked as on the slide.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally descending a slope as skiers do, and idiomatically getting worse with age.

clue.text: Holiday accommodation: it's found in outskirts of Grenoble

indicators.note: the word it sits within the letters taken from the city
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A travel guide notes a holiday let on the edge of a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: The outskirts of Grenoble are G and E; IT goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A French rural holiday home let to tourists is known by this word.

clue.text: Friend tucked in, showing taste

parts.note: a pal is a friend
to tuck in is to eat heartily, so tucked in is ate

explanation.surface: A friend eating heartily shows discernment about food.
explanation.definitionFit: The sense of flavour, or discerning taste in food, is a standard synonym.

clue.text: Composer's work introduced to Eastern land shortly

indicators.note: the work abbreviation is put into the shortened country
shortly means cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: China is a land in the East
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A composer's piece is brought briefly to an Oriental country.
explanation.definitionFit: The Polish Romantic pianist and writer of nocturnes is a famous composer.

clue.text: Track first of patients at hospital

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word patients is taken

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Monitoring the earliest patients arriving at hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A track or trail is a synonym for a way along which one walks.

clue.text: Put off storing metal receptacle as container for wine

indicators.note: the word for put off stores the receptacle inside itself

parts.note: to deter is to put off or discourage
a can is a metal receptacle

explanation.surface: Someone is discouraged from keeping wine in a tin rather than a proper vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass vessel into which wine is poured to settle before serving.

clue.text: Socialising at university is confusing

parts.note: mixing means socialising with others
UP means in residence at university, as in going up to Oxford

explanation.surface: Student social life is bewildering.
explanation.definitionFit: To muddle things together is to confuse them; the phrasal verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Warehouseman has secured employment

indicators.note: the long word holds the answer secured within its letters

explanation.surface: A warehouse worker has found himself a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Employment in the sense of utilisation, putting something to work, is a synonym.

clue.text: GP mentioned leaf to relieve nettle sting

indicators.note: mentioned signals a word spoken, so it is a sound-alike

parts.note: a GP, general practitioner, is a doctor, informally a doc

explanation.surface: A family doctor recommends a leaf to soothe nettle stings.
explanation.walkthrough: A GP is a British family doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: The broad-leaved weed traditionally rubbed on skin stung by nettles.

clue.text: Tories beat left in the end: it's always the same

parts.note: Cons is short for Conservatives, the Tories
to tan someone's hide is to beat them

indicators.note: the final letter of the word left is taken

explanation.surface: A political commentator says the Conservatives defeating the left is unchanging.
explanation.definitionFit: Unvarying, never changing, is the adjective's core sense.

clue.text: Part of castle? Look around

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the word for look is read backwards

parts.note: to peek is to take a quick look

explanation.surface: A tourist asks about a castle's features and is told to explore.
explanation.definitionFit: The strongest central tower of a castle, its donjon, has this name.

clue.text: Sports side departed, getting victory against fourth in league

parts.note: having departed is having left
a win is a victory

indicators.note: the fourth letter of the word league is taken

explanation.surface: A team leaves after beating the side placed fourth in the table.
explanation.definitionFit: In football or hockey a wing is a flank of the pitch, and the left one is a playing side.

clue.text: Maybe Prime Minister arranged deal with sovereign

indicators.note: the letters of deal are arranged in a new order

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, a sovereign

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister may have struck a deal with the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A Prime Minister is one example of the head of a government or party.

clue.text: Join parade and collapse

definitions.meaning: soldiers take their place in the ranks on a parade ground
a roof can cave in or give way

explanation.definitionFit: The military order to line up on parade, and the phrasal verb for a structure caving in.

clue.text: Gosh! North-west is linked to entire South-west region of England

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like gosh
N and W are the compass abbreviations for north and west
all means entire

explanation.surface: An exclaimed geography note links a corner of the country to the whole south-west.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a Cockney-style exclamation like 'gosh'.
explanation.definitionFit: The county at the far south-western tip of England, beyond Devon.

clue.text: Paints dilapidated silo

indicators.note: dilapidated means in ruins, so the letters of the farm tower are knocked into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone paints a run-down grain store.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil paints, or artworks made with them, are referred to by this plural.

clue.text: Dislike cheap ties, every other one

indicators.note: every other letter of the two words is taken, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Someone loathes tacky neckwear, every single one.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong dislike or loathing is a synonym.

clue.text: Claim walker is overwhelmed by drink

indicators.note: the walker word is engulfed by the drink word around it

parts.note: ale is a beer, a drink
a leg is what one walks with

explanation.surface: A hiker is said to have been drowned in booze.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert something without proof is to claim it.

clue.text: Lewis, perhaps, is name adopted by boy

indicators.note: the name abbreviation is taken in by the boy word

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy has taken on the name Lewis.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis is in the Outer Hebrides off Scotland; 'Lewis' looks like a person's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis is one example of a landmass surrounded by sea.
